extracted.intended_audience: Researchers submitting or evaluating Registered Reports at Peer Community In (authors, recommenders/editors, and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and public record for evaluation and recommendation of Registered Reports on the PCI Registered Reports platform, covering Stage 1 in-principle acceptance (IPA), Stage 2 recommendations, bias-control level reporting, preregistration links, and publication options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 criteria (In-principle acceptance, IPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript met the Stage 1 criteria and therefore awarded in-principle acceptance (IPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page indicate Stage 1 acceptances are given after evaluation (sometimes over multiple rounds) and are associated with: transparent preregistration (URL to the Stage 1 protocol), detailed analysis plans and outcome-neutral criteria, methodological rigor, explicit statements about bias control (a reported 'Level of bias control achieved'), and considered responses to reviewers' and recommender's comments. The site repeatedly reports 'The Stage 1 manuscript was evaluated over X rounds of review. Based on detailed responses to the reviewers' and recommender's comments, the recommender judged that the manuscript met the Stage 1 criteria and therefore awarded in-principle acceptance (IPA).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 criteria (Positive recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 2 manuscript was evaluated and judged to have met the Stage 2 criteria and awarded a positive recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 2 entries state the manuscript 'met the Stage 2 criteria and awarded a positive recommendation' typically after one or more rounds of review and after authors' responses and revisions. Stage 2 evaluation is reported alongside the preregistered protocol URL and the previously reported bias-control level. The page implies Stage 2 assessment requires that authors have completed the planned work per the accepted Stage 1 protocol and addressed reviewers' concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of bias control achieved (overall metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each record reports a 'Level of bias control achieved' (a numbered level) describing the extent to which data/evidence were controlled relative to IPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page shows that authors must state the Level of bias control achieved and gives explicit definitions for levels (examples of Level 2, 3, 4, 6 appear on the page). This reported level is used as part of the record for the Registered Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 6 (bias control)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No part of the data or evidence that was used to answer the research question was generated until after IPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 4 (bias control)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least some of the data/evidence that was used to answer the research question already existed and was accessible in principle to the authors prior to Stage 1 IPA, but the authors certify that they had not yet accessed any part of that data/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 3 (bias control)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least some data/evidence that was used to the answer the research question had been accessed by the authors prior to in-principle acceptance (e.g. downloaded or otherwise received), but the authors certify that they had not yet observed any part of the data/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 2 (bias control)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least some data that was used to answer the research question had been accessed and partially observed by the authors prior to Stage 1 in-principle acceptance, but the authors certify that they had not yet observed the key variables within the data that were used to answer the research question and they took additional steps to maximise bias control and rigour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of URL to preregistered Stage 1 protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Each record includes a 'URL to the preregistered Stage 1 protocol'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page displays a direct link to the Stage 1 protocol (e.g. an OSF URL) for each Registered Report, indicating that providing the preregistered protocol URL is expected and is part of the public record for PCI RR evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed analysis plans and outcome-neutral criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 submissions are expected to include detailed analysis plans and outcome-neutral criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Burns et al. entry commends the submission for being 'transparently preregistered, with detailed analysis plans and outcome-neutral criteria.' This phrasing indicates that such plans and pre-specified, outcome-neutral decision rules are key evaluative features for Stage 1 acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly specified thresholds / decision rules for hypothesis confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses should specify thresholds or decision rules for confirming hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Burns et al. example notes planned quantification 'with clearly specified thresholds for confirming their hypotheses' (e.g. thresholds for Dice coefficient differences or reliability-corrected correlations). The page therefore treats clear, pre-specified decision thresholds as an important criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological rigor and transparent preregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological rigor and transparency in preregistration are required/valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple records are described as 'methodologically rigorous' and 'transparently preregistered.' Items highlighted include theoretically grounded designs, well-specified methods, preregistered sequential sampling plans, exclusion criteria, and planned analyses — all used by recommenders when judging Stage 1/2 criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' responses to reviewers' and recommender's comments (revisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must provide considered responses and revisions addressing reviewers' and recommender's comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Across many entries the page records that decisions (IPA or positive recommendation) followed 'detailed responses to the reviewers' and recommender's comments' and, in several cases, multiple rounds of review. This procedural requirement is repeatedly presented as part of meeting Stage 1/Stage 2 criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of eligible PCI-RR-friendly journals / publication options
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR records list 'eligible PCI-RR-friendly journals' and publication options for recommended Registered Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states RRs positively evaluated by PCI RR 'are publicly recommended and can be left as is, published directly in Peer Community Journal, or submitted to PCI RR-friendly journals (see the list here) or other journals.' Each record prints a list of eligible journals (examples include Peer Community Journal, PeerJ, Royal Society Open Science, etc.), indicating acceptable publication venues or onward submission options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission guidance (read guides & policies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting a preprint, authors should read the guide for authors, how PCI RR works, and guidelines for recommenders and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The top of the page instructs: 'Before submitting a preprint, please carefully read the guide for authors, how PCI RR works, and find out what you can do with a PCI RR-recommended preprint. You may also want to check out the guidelines for recommenders and reviewers.' This is presented as required preparatory guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright / Licensing policy for published texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of comments, reviews and recommendations retain copyright under specific Creative Commons licenses depending on date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states: 'Authors of comments, reviews and recommendations retain copyright© under CC-BY for texts published after and including 24/01/2022 and under CC-BY-ND before.' This legal/policy information is part of the platform's publication standards.
